issues.description: Attribute 'animals' in class Farm: the problem statement and UML explicitly require a List<Animal> implemented using an ArrayList and initialized in a no-arg constructor, but the provided solution declares the field as a Set<Animal> and initializes it with a HashSet. The template Farm.java currently contains a TODO placeholder for implementing the collection. This discrepancy between the specification (List/ArrayList) and the solution implementation (Set/HashSet) creates ambiguity for students about which collection type to use and may lead to inconsistent implementations or mismatches with tests that expect an ArrayList/List API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the solution to declare the field as a List<Animal> and initialize it as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor (e.g., private List<Animal> animals; this.animals = new ArrayList<>();) to match the UML/problem statement and teaching intent. Alternatively, if a Set is intentional, update the problem statement/UML to state that a Set (HashSet) is acceptable and explain why a Set is chosen.
